summary: de Matos et al. 2023 (HypnoScience project, fMRI, N=50): hypnosis produces robust changes in functional connectome (parieto-occipital-temporal, cuneal/precuneal, lingual gyri); depth-dependent changes between two hypnotic states; lingual gyrus = lowest common denominator (confirms Landry).
content: de Matos et al. (2023, Front Hum Neurosci, HypnoScience fMRI study, N=50 hypnosis-experienced). Whole-brain MVPA comparing 2 hypnotic states (differing in depth) vs matched controls. Key hubs: parieto-occipital-temporal areas, cuneal/precuneal, occipital cortices, lingual gyri, occipital pole. Direct comparison of the two hypnotic states revealed depth-dependent connectivity changes (left superior temporal/supramarginal gyri, cuneus, planum temporale, lingual gyri). Lingual gyrus involved in ALL statistical comparisons — supports Landry meta-analysis 'lowest common denominator' finding. Authors: 'neural correlates of hypnotic states HS1 and HS2 strongly overlap when compared to respective control states.' Respiration rate significantly slowed during hypnosis. Provides further evidence of hypnotic depth-dependent connectivity differences (cf. McGeown 2015).
